original_question: For the class of pure O-sequences, if two sequences agree in every entry except one and the differing entries differ by a positive integer alpha, must every intermediate value also occur in a pure O-sequence? In particular, does this Interval Conjecture for Pure O-sequences remain true in three variables?
target_in_paper: Section 2’s discussion of the Interval Property as specialized to pure O-sequences (the ICP), together with Theorem 2.16 and the immediately following remark that the conjecture remains open in three variables, while a four-variable counterexample is given in Example 2.17.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s Interval Conjecture for Pure O-sequences: two pure O-sequences agree in every entry except one, their differing entry differs by a positive integer alpha, and one asks whether all intermediate values also occur. It also correctly singles out the unresolved three-variable/codimension-3 case mentioned in the paper.
missing_details: A pure O-sequence should be defined explicitly as an h-vector h=(1,h_1,...,h_e) of a finite monomial order ideal closed under divisibility, whose maximal monomials all have the same degree.
The ambient algebraic equivalent is implicit in the draft: pure O-sequences are exactly Hilbert functions of standard graded Artinian monomial level algebras.
The socle degree e should be named, since the paper’s main positive theorem for the ICP is stated for socle degree e<=3.

The index of the modified entry should be quantified explicitly. In the unrestricted ICP it is some i with 1<=i<=e; in the codimension-3 reformulation, h_1=3 is fixed, so the varying index should be i>=2.
The formal interval statement should specify the beta-range explicitly: beta=0,1,...,alpha (equivalently, the nontrivial intermediate cases are 1<=beta<=alpha-1).
For the three-variable case, the paper means codimension 3 / h_1=3, not merely an ambient ring that happens to have at most three variables.
The field issue is omitted: the paper notes that whether a sequence is a pure O-sequence is independent of the choice of field K.
The draft does not record the paper’s proved partial result that the ICP holds for all pure O-sequences of socle degree at most 3, in any number of variables.
The paper-faithful context also distinguishes the status by codimension: still open in three variables, but already disproved in four variables in the cited example.
refined_question: Does the Interval Conjecture for Pure O-sequences hold in codimension 3? Precisely: let h=(1,3,h_2,...,h_e) be the h-vector of a finite pure monomial order ideal in K[y_1,y_2,y_3] (equivalently, a pure O-sequence of codimension 3, with socle degree e). If, for some index i with 2<=i<=e and some integer alpha>0, both (1,3,h_2,...,h_i,...,h_e) and (1,3,h_2,...,h_i+alpha,...,h_e) are pure O-sequences, must every intermediate sequence (1,3,h_2,...,h_i+beta,...,h_e) with beta=0,1,...,alpha also be a pure O-sequence? The paper proves this interval property for socle degree e<=3 in arbitrary codimension; is it true without any bound on e when the codimension is 3?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does the interval property hold for Hilbert functions of standard graded Artinian monomial level algebras of codimension 3: if two such Hilbert functions differ only in one degree by alpha>0, are all intermediate Hilbert functions again realized by Artinian monomial level algebras?
justification: The draft is targeting the ICP, not a broader problem about arbitrary level or Gorenstein Hilbert functions. In the survey, the authors first define pure O-sequences and their algebraic interpretation, then state the general interval-property template and apply it to pure O-sequences, prove it for socle degree at most 3, and immediately note that the three-variable case is still open while the four-variable case fails. So the sharpest stand-alone reformulation keeps the exact one-entry interpolation question, adds the missing definitions and quantifiers, and narrows the open part to codimension 3, which is the unresolved case the draft is pointing at.
